title: AI Model Photos and Videos for Fashion Brands | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI model photos and videos for fashion brands from garment photos laid flat or on a hanger: on-body shots, lookbook scenes, and outfit reels.
h1: AI Model Photos and Videos for Fashion Brands and Boutiques
lead: For fashion catalogs, combine on-model previews with garment detail photos, collection scenes, and short outfit videos from your product photos.
card: Garment photos to on-model views, lookbook scenes, and short outfit clips.
intro: Clothing shoppers compare hem length, fabric drape, print, and what to pair with a piece. Photos of a garment laid flat or on a hanger show its cut; an on-model view adds a styling reference, which shoppers can compare with the listed measurements.

Upload a clean photo of the garment and describe how it should be worn: walking down a city street, seated on a stool in a bright studio, or styled as a full look for a lookbook page. For motion, a short vertical clip of someone turning in the outfit shows swing and drape in a way a still can't. On-model photos give a collection a consistent way to show the cut. Let your size chart and measurements do the job of explaining fit.

ideas.d: Style a trench coat on a rainy street or a sundress on a boardwalk for a collection page, a newsletter, or Instagram posts announcing the drop.
A 6- to 15-second vertical clip of the outfit turning, walking, or sitting shows movement. Add music and captions afterward in TikTok or CapCut.
Ask for a styled image with open space to one side, then type your discount and end date over it in Canva or Ads Manager so the numbers are exactly right.

faq.q: Can I turn a photo of a garment laid flat into an on-model photo?
faq.a: Yes. Lay the garment flat or hang it on a plain wall, smooth out the wrinkles, and photograph the whole piece in even light. Then describe the person and setting, for example "full-length, standing in a bright studio."

faq.q: Will the AI change my print or fabric?
faq.a: It works from your photo, so fine stripes, embroidery, and buttons hold up when the upload is sharp and close. Look carefully at patterns and trims before you list the image, and make another version if anything has drifted.

faq.q: Can I show my clothes on a plus-size or petite model?
faq.a: You can describe the person you want to see, including height, build, and age range, such as "petite woman in her 40s" or "tall man with a broad frame." Showing your real customer helps shoppers picture themselves in the piece.

faq.q: How do I make a TikTok video of my clothes being worn?
faq.a: Choose 9:16 and a length of 6, 10, or 15 seconds, then describe a slow turn or short walk. Run another version when you want a different setting.

overview.h2: Show the cut, then show the life around it

items.t: Give the garment a dependable starting point
items.d: Photograph the whole piece laid flat or hanging, then add a close view of any print, embroidery, hardware, or unusual hem. A clean source helps the result keep the details that make the item yours.
An on-body image can show styling, length, and the mood of a collection. Keep your size chart, garment measurements, and fabric notes beside it; a generated model cannot replace those references.
Lay a dress, shirt, trouser, or coat flat with sleeves and hems visible, or hang it against a plain wall. Do not crop off straps, cuffs, or pockets.
Use a second photo for the back when the back panel, hood, split, or pocket changes the silhouette. The model cannot show an unseen construction detail reliably.
Add a close crop for knit, denim, embroidery, sequins, or a fine print. Soft, even light helps the texture stay legible without hard shadows.
Decide whether the garment should be tucked, belted, layered, or loose before you write the scene. Describe one complete outfit instead of several competing looks.
Store chest, waist, rise, inseam, length, and size-chart information in your listing. Use the generated image to show styling, not to promise a particular fit.
A full-length model in a bright studio wearing the black linen dress, standing still with the hem and sleeves fully visible against a pale wall.
A cropped denim jacket over a white tee, walking past a brick storefront with the jacket open so the collar, pockets, and back yoke show.
A tailored blazer over a knit top at a café table, then a close crop of the cuff and button beside a notebook.
Three hoodies in charcoal, oat, and forest green folded on the same bench, one person lifting the forest green version to show the front graphic.

results.h2: What a clothing set can include

items.d: Use an on-body frame beside your photo of the garment laid flat and a detail photo so shoppers connect silhouette with construction.
A consistent lookbook scene lets pieces share light, crop, and styling language.
Choose 9:16 for an outfit reel, 1:1 for a feed, or 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 for a wider or taller placement; clip lengths are 6, 10, or 15 seconds.
The preview displays the credit cost before you start, so you can choose a photo or clip with the scope that suits the outfit.
For commercial-use and watermark guidance, read the [FAQ](/faq) before using a file.
Compare cuffs, buttons, pockets, print placement, and the number of garments with your sample before publishing.
Place measurements, fabric composition, size availability, sale price, and end date in your store or ad editor.
AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions; place approved size details and channel text in your editor after download.

fit.h2: When this approach fits a fashion range

good.d: Dresses, tops, trousers, outerwear, knitwear, and accessories photographed in full.
Pieces that benefit from a location, layered outfit, or consistent lookbook treatment.
Multiple versions that can share one composition while retaining their own product photos.

not_ideal.d: Use real measurements and sample photography for stretch, compression, or a precise size promise.
